name: sgs/nav-bar-menu
title: SGS Nav Bar Menu
description: The site's primary navigation BAR — a flat horizontal row of real links on desktop; below the collapse point it becomes a burger that opens the menu panel (an sgs/nav-drawer holding an sgs/nav-drawer-menu list) via the shared sgs/nav Interactivity store. Renders dropdowns and mega panels. Menu content comes from a native WordPress menu.

indicator.reason: style.css declares .sgs-nav-bar-menu__indicator { pointer-events: none; } — the element is structurally unhoverable, the browser passes all pointer events through to whatever is underneath. It paints from the item Background row's own Hover swatch (itemBgHover / itemBgHoverGradient) under itemBgHoverTreatment === 'highlight' (Spec 41 FR-41-25), so its colour already carries that row's states rather than a parallel pair of its own.

submenu-bg.reason: The submenu panel's visibility is a binary open/closed disclosure toggled by the trigger, not by pointer position over the panel itself — once open, the pointer is always over some interactive CHILD, never a hoverable moment on the panel background itself. The hoverable surface inside the panel is the LINK background, which carries its own full three-state family (submenuLinkBg / submenuLinkBgHover / submenuLinkBgCurrent, Spec 41 FR-41-9) — that is where a hover fill belongs, and it is declared there.

submenu-border.reason: The panel's border sits on the same structurally non-hoverable surface as its background, for the same reason: once the panel is open the pointer is always over an interactive CHILD. Per-state border colour inside the panel belongs to the LINK, whose own three-state family (submenuLinkBg / submenuLinkBgHover / submenuLinkBgCurrent) is where a pointer-driven change is actually perceivable. submenuBorderColour is therefore Normal-only (Spec 41 FR-41-9).

scrim.label: Backdrop / scrim
scrim._note: The shared viewport scrim (Wave 3C U-2, `includes/helpers-scrim.php::sgs_scrim_render`): the see-through layer printed at wp_footer that dims the page while this block's drawer, dialog or panel is open. Mapped here so the converter can route a draft's scrim colour, strength and blur to these attributes.

wrapper.label: Nav wrapper
wrapper._note: The rendered <nav> (block-private root, no SGS_Container_Wrapper). Padding/margin ride the native spacing support; max-width is the flat attribute. navBg/navColour/navBgHover all write to the same bare $uid_sel wrapper selector. The remaining ARRANGEMENT members (layer OUTER) — display/flex-direction/align-items etc. — are honest GAPs: style.css hardcodes `display:flex;align-items:center` with no attribute behind it; its `justify-content:space-between` default sits in `:where()` and yields to the `justifyContent` attribute.
wrapper._note_hover_nav: navColourHover is routed to the wrapper element because render.php emits sgs_hover_state_rules( "{$uid_sel}", 'color:…', ':focus-visible' ) on the block ROOT, not a descendant.

bar.label: Item bar (flex row)
bar._note: The <ul class="sgs-nav-bar-menu__bar"> that actually arranges the item links — distinct from `wrapper`, which arranges the bar against the burger toggle-wrap. Remaining ARRANGEMENT members are honest GAPs (style.css hardcodes `display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap` with no attribute). This block declares no `listColumns` grid-column-count destination; that attribute belongs to the in-drawer vertical list on sgs/nav-drawer-menu.

item.label: Nav item (resting)

hover._noBaseByDesignNote: css:padding-inline-start (itemPaddingShiftHover) has no resting counterpart by design: the value is an ADDITIVE hover-only shift on top of whatever inline-start padding is already in effect at rest (style.css's `padding: 8px 12px`), not an absolute padding of its own — a 'resting shift' control would be redundant with the item's existing padding. Same shape as css:transform (scaleHover) on sgs/icon/sgs/post-grid, Bean-ruled 2026-08-20.

item._note: The nav item LINK — every stateful control on this element targets the <a>, never the <li> (Spec 41 FR-41-1). Three states are declared: base, `hover` (render.php's `$hover_targets` = `:hover, :focus-visible`) and `current` (`[aria-current="page"]`), so a visitor can distinguish WHERE THEY ARE from WHAT THEY ARE POINTING AT. The current-page state is operator-controllable through `itemColourCurrent` / `itemBgCurrent` / `itemFontWeightCurrent` (Spec 41 FR-41-1); `itemFontWeightCurrent` is the non-colour signal that satisfies WCAG 1.4.1 without relying on colour alone. `current` deliberately maps DIFFERENT attribute names from `hover`: the classifier's `extract-signatures.py::_record` is last-write-wins, so a state map byte-identical to `hover` silently overwrites the hover derivation and tags those attributes with a css_state they never render in. Every state member is EXPLICIT rather than left to the `{prefix}Suffix` convention — `css:font-weight`, `css:text-decoration` and `css:text-transform` each carry a base attribute AND a state sibling, and without an explicit entry per state both derive to the same (property, element, state=NULL) slot and collide on one routing destination. The base `css:font-weight` -> `itemFontWeight` entry is load-bearing for the same reason: a state entry with no base is the STATE_WITHOUT_BASE shape the manifest gate flags. `css:border-radius` -> `itemBorderRadius` is base-only — radius has no state on `SgsBorderControl` (Spec 41 FR-41-7). M-21 (2026-09-23): `css:opacity` -> itemOpacity/itemOpacityHover and `css:padding-inline-start` -> itemPaddingShiftHover (hover-only) added; itemPaddingShiftHover is ALSO mapped on the `sublink` element below (dropdown/mega submenu link) — the SAME attribute reused across both elements, deliberately, because the reference sites (halcyon minimal, indus-foods dropdown) only ever set one padding-shift value per instance, never two different ones at once; itemOpacity/itemOpacityHover are NOT reused on `sublink` because fantasy's own reference needs a genuinely DIFFERENT rest/hover opacity pair on its sub-link (0.6 to 1) from its item link (1 to 0.5) — reusing the same attribute there would apply the wrong number to one of the two elements.

indicator.label: Sliding indicator
indicator._note: The `.sgs-nav-bar-menu__indicator` sliding pill, view.js-animated behind the active/hovered item. It is rendered under `itemBgHoverTreatment === 'highlight'` and paints from the item Background row's OWN Hover swatch — `itemBgHover` / `itemBgHoverGradient`, claimed by the `item` element's `states.hover` (Spec 41 FR-41-25) — so this element routes no attribute of its own: one picker, one property, three ways of applying it. `clusters: ["fill"]` is retained (not `[]`) because the forward-resolution pass only visits a cluster's members when the cluster is declared; with an empty attrMap the fill members are honest GAPs, ungated and correct, since this element has no controls of its own. `supports.sgs.colourExemptions.indicator` records why it carries no hover state: style.css declares `.sgs-nav-bar-menu__indicator { pointer-events: none; }`, so the element is structurally unhoverable.

item-separator.label: Item separator (bar)
item-separator._note: FR-41-37. The between-item vertical rule on the horizontal bar (nav-menu-css.php's item-separator block) -- a GENUINELY SEPARATE element from `item` (the link itself): this rule paints on the <li> (`.sgs-nav-bar-menu__item::after` when Sweep is active) or via longhand border-right-* on the <a>'s existing border box otherwise, never the item's own itemBorderColour/itemBorderWidth family (see nav-menu-css.php's own comment distinguishing the two). Longhand border-right-* declared explicitly (not the `border-color`/`border-width` shorthand `item` uses) because a shorthand here would reset whatever the item's own underline/row-separator family already wrote on the SAME selector when Sweep is off. `itemSeparatorHoverTreatment`/`itemSeparatorSweepAngle` are declared `role:behaviour` (attr-classification-overrides.json) rather than routed through this manifest -- they are control-selector/parameter attrs, not paintable CSS values, matching the pattern for itemBorderHoverTreatment on the `item` element above.

featured.label: Featured item
featured._note: featuredFontWeightHover is a genuine hover-state weight change (only emitted when it differs from resting), declared under `text` cluster's css:font-weight member. featuredColourGradient mirrors burgerColourGradient's shape -- explicit attrMap since css:color-gradient is not resolved by the default {prefix}Suffix convention, same reason burgerColourGradient needed one. Resting LABEL form only; PILL form and the submenu-inheritance custom property stay flat (see render.php comments). featuredBgGradient/featuredBgHoverGradient: non-empty wins over the resolved featuredBg/featuredBgHover slug+hex; when active the pill foreground skips WCAG contrast-against-background maths (no single hex to test) and uses the operator's own flat colour instead (see render.php). The submenu-inheritance custom property stays hex-only, same scope boundary as featuredColourGradient above.

badge.label: Item badge
badge._note: Wave B. The optional per-item marker chip ("SOON", "NEW") rendered after an item's or sublink's label via includes/nav-menu-markup.php::sgs_nav_shared_badge_html(). Badge COPY is per-item (the operator's WordPress classic-menu-item Description field, repurposed -- see that function's own docblock); badge COLOUR is block-level, one Colour-panel row applying to every badge this bar renders, matching sgs/cart's badgeColour/badgeTextColour precedent (sgs-db.py: sgs/cart badgeColour default "accent", badgeTextColour default "accent-text"). No hover state -- a badge is never itself interactive. Zero-specificity `:where()` default in style.css paints a neutral accent-light/accent-text chip when an operator has not touched either attribute; render.php's own #uid-scoped rule (specificity 0,2,0) always wins over it.

burger.label: Burger toggle
burger._note: burgerColour is the icon TEXT colour (css:color); burgerHoverColour drives the button's HOVER background-color; burgerBg is its resting counterpart (a base attribute with an inspector control in the edit.js Burger panel, Normal state), so css:background-color resolves at base too. Unset burgerBg leaves style.css's `background:none` default. `css:color`->burgerColour, `css:background-color`->burgerBg and `states.hover.css:color`->burgerColourHover (sgs_hover_state_rules on `:hover, :focus-visible`) are declared EXPLICITLY, because burgerColour and burgerColourHover would otherwise both derive to (color, burger, state=NULL) and collide on one routing slot -- the hover entry is what separates them. The manifest is the durable source for these routings. Spec 35 §12 audit item 5 (2026-09-24) added the `motion` cluster (already defined in cluster-member-sets.json with exactly these two members, nothing new invented) + explicit attrMap entries for burgerMorphDuration/burgerMorphEasing -- the default {prefix}{suffix} convention would resolve them to 'burgerDuration'/'burgerEasing' (prefix 'burger' + suffix 'Duration'/'Easing'), which do not match the real attribute names (burgerMorphDuration/burgerMorphEasing), so an explicit attrMap entry is required, not optional.

sublink.label: Submenu link

hover._noBaseByDesignNote: css:padding-inline-start (itemPaddingShiftHover, M-21) has no resting counterpart by design: an ADDITIVE hover-only shift on top of the resting inline-start padding already in effect (includes/nav-menu-submenu-css.php's hardcoded `padding:0 16px`, no attribute of its own to override). Reused from the `item` element above -- see that element's own note for why the SAME attribute (not a separate submenuPaddingShiftHover) is correct here.

sublink._note: The submenu LINK — <a class="sgs-nav-bar-menu__sublink">, painted at render.php's own scoped `.sgs-nav-bar-menu__sublink{...}` rule. It carries three states: base, `hover` (`sgs_hover_state_rules()` on `:hover, :focus-visible`) and `current` (`[aria-current="page"]`), matching the bar item's own three-state model (Spec 41 FR-41-1 / FR-41-9). `"prefix": ""` is a deliberate, permanent opt-out from the `{prefix}Suffix` convention: a `submenu` prefix would wrongly claim submenuAlign/Caret/CloseGrace/MinWidth/Padding and the whole submenuBorder* family, which belong to the submenu PANEL (the `submenu-panel` element) rather than to this anchor. The `submenu`-prefixed typography attributes that DO belong to this anchor reach it through the explicit attrMap entries above, one per property — that is the resolution, not a prefix (Spec 41 FR-41-22c). With an empty prefix nothing here resolves by convention, so every member is explicit by necessity: each state's `css:color`, `css:background-color`, `css:font-weight`, `css:text-decoration` and `css:text-transform` names a DIFFERENT attribute from its base sibling, because without an explicit entry a base and its state sibling both derive to (property, sublink, state=NULL) and collide on one routing slot. `"fill"` is declared alongside `"text"` so the forward-resolution pass actually visits css:background-color / css:background-image and consults this attrMap; a cluster that is not declared is never iterated. submenuColourGradient is routed as a DIRECT declaration (sgs_text_colour_decl / sgs_resolve_text_colour_or_gradient) rather than a colour-valued custom property, because a `var(--x, …)` chain feeding a fixed `color:` declaration cannot switch to `background-image` for a gradient (survey.js's `paints-via-colour-valued-custom-property`  submenuOpacity/submenuOpacityHover (M-21, this task) close the fantasy reference gap left open by the item element's own opacity pair — fantasy needs the sublink resting at 0.6 opacity and brightening to 1 on hover, the OPPOSITE direction from the item's 1-to-0.5, so a genuinely separate attribute pair was required rather than reusing itemOpacity/itemOpacityHover here.

submenu-panel.label: Submenu panel
submenu-panel._note: The floating dropdown PANEL — <div class="sgs-nav-bar-menu__submenu"> — as distinct from the links inside it, which are the `sublink` element (Spec 41 FR-41-9). Base only: NO `states` key at all, because the panel has neither a hover nor a current state for any property. Its visibility is a binary open/closed disclosure toggled by the trigger; once open the pointer is always over an interactive CHILD, so a pointer-driven change on the panel surface itself is never perceivable — the hoverable surface inside the panel is the LINK background (submenuLinkBg / submenuLinkBgHover / submenuLinkBgCurrent on `sublink`). Recorded as `supports.sgs.colourExemptions.submenu-bg` and `.submenu-border`. `"prefix": ""` for the same reason `sublink` carries it: a `submenu` prefix would claim submenuColour* and the submenu typography family, which belong to the LINK. Every member is therefore explicit.

disabled-item.label: Disabled item
disabled-item._note: Wave B, 2026-09-24. A disabled menu item renders as non-link text with aria-disabled="true" (render.php's own selector). Declared as its own element, NOT as a `disabled` state on `item`: `disabled` is not in golden-controls.json _meta.stateVocabulary (hover/current/scrolled; admission is Bean-approved), and declaring it as a state raised the required state count on every item colour row.

sgs._note_sweep_eligibility: The ONE declarative source for the Sweep-treatment eligibility predicate, read by BOTH surfaces — edit.js decides whether to offer the Sweep segment, render.php decides whether to emit Sweep CSS — with neither re-deriving the rule (Spec 41 FR-41-26). It is NOT an `elements` entry and routes no CSS property; it sits beside colourExemptions / hideExtensions / boxFamilies. Three keys per row: `blockingBackgroundAttrs` (Sweep is withdrawn when ANY named attribute is non-empty, because background-clip:text clips the element's whole background-painting area to the glyph shapes — every state's background counts, not just the resting one), `blockingGradientAttrs` (the row's own text gradient writes background-image on the identical selector, so whichever loses is invisible) and `glyphGuard` (background-clip:text needs glyphs to grip; null means the element always has them). Every attribute named below must exist in `attributes` — a typo reads as permanently empty, so the predicate would always pass and the rule would silently cease to exist.

attributes._note_nav_fill: Nav CONTAINER surface. Scope is deliberately SURFACE ONLY (navBg / navColour and their Hover siblings): border, radius and divider are not offered here because the pill-nav and bordered-nav patterns that justify them are whole-HEADER treatments, and sgs/site-header already declares `color` + `__experimentalBorder` supports for exactly that. Do not add them here without a header-level reason. Defaults are unset, so an untouched nav paints no surface of its own. Because the drawer holds its OWN sgs/nav-drawer-menu instance, that block's identical attributes give fully independent drawer styling with no extra plumbing.

navColourGradient.description: CSS gradient string painting the nav text with a background-clip:text mechanism instead of a flat colour. Non-empty wins over navColour. Safe unconditionally -- navBg already paints on a separate ::after layer (sgs_block_background_layer_css()), never this same selector.

itemColourGradient.description: CSS gradient string painting the resting nav-item text with a background-clip:text mechanism instead of a flat colour. Non-empty wins over itemColour. Safe unconditionally -- itemBg already paints on a ::before layer, never this same selector. See itemColourHoverGradient for the Hover-state sibling.

itemBgGradient.description: CSS gradient string painting the resting nav-item background via the same ::before layer as itemBg; non-empty wins over the flat itemBg colour, mirroring itemColourGradient's sibling-wins pattern.

itemColourHoverGradient.description: CSS gradient string painting the Hover-state nav-item text, mirroring itemColourGradient's background-clip:text mechanism. Non-empty wins over itemColourHover. Offered in the editor ONLY while itemSmartContrast is OFF (the default) -- when itemSmartContrast is ON, itemColourHover auto-computes a safe solid colour for WCAG contrast against itemBgHover, which a gradient cannot meaningfully replace, so a stored value here is ignored by render.php while the swap is active rather than silently reappearing.

featuredColourGradient.description: CSS gradient string painting the featured bar item's LABEL-form text with a background-clip:text mechanism instead of a flat colour (mirrors burgerColourGradient). Non-empty wins over featuredColour. Resting LABEL form only (no featuredBg set) -- the PILL form (featuredBg set) keeps its WCAG-contrast-resolved flat foreground, and the submenu inheritance custom property (--sgs-nm-featured-colour) stays flat-only because its consumer paints a background on the same selector (see render.php).

featuredBgGradient.description: CSS gradient string painting the featured item's PILL-form background (background-image custom-property-gradient pattern). Non-empty wins over the resolved featuredBg slug/hex. When active, the pill's foreground SKIPS the WCAG contrast-against-background computation (sgs_wcag_preferred_text_colour_for_bg() needs ONE background hex; a gradient has none) and uses the operator's own FLAT featuredColour/featuredColourHover choice instead -- never the gradient-capable text resolve, which would collide with this same background-image on the same selector (see render.php comment at the featured-item paint block, and featuredColourGradient's note above for the identical precedent on the flat-hex pill form). The submenu-inherited featured item (--sgs-nm-featured-bg custom property) is NOT extended to carry this gradient -- same documented scope boundary as featuredColourGradient's submenu gap above.

featuredBgHoverGradient.description: CSS gradient string painting the featured item's PILL-form :hover/:focus-visible background (mirrors featuredBgGradient). Non-empty wins over the resolved featuredBgHover slug/hex. Same WCAG-skip rationale as featuredBgGradient: the hover foreground uses the operator's own flat featuredColourHover (falling back to featuredColour) rather than computing WCAG contrast against a gradient.

burgerFontSize.description: Spec 41 Wave 2 J1. Unset renders font-size:inherit (helpers-typography.php's sgs_typography_css_rule(), $inherit_font_size_when_blank) — inherits the theme's real body font-size rather than the UA <button> default (~13.3px).

burgerFontFamily.description: Spec 41 Wave 2 J1. Unset renders font-family:inherit ($inherit_font_family_when_blank) — inherits the theme's real body font rather than the UA default (Arial).

burgerLetterSpacing.description: Tier object mirroring submenuLetterSpacing's shape. Default resolves to 0.05em (see burgerLetterSpacingUnit).

itemMagnetStrength.description: Wave 3C U-11 (M-10). The item magnet's pull FACTOR, 0.02 to 0.5. No default — unset means today's exact behaviour: `view.js::initBarEffects` calls `initMagnet(el)` with no options at all, giving `magnet.js`'s own shipped defaults (factor 0.15, an 8px cap). When set, the cap is lifted (`maxPull: Infinity`) — the pointer only ever engages while inside the item's own box (the listener is on the item), so the pull is naturally bounded by half the item's width times the factor, matching what halcyon (0.16) and indus-foods (0.14) actually measure. Shown only while `itemMagnetEnabled` is on.

burgerMorph.description: Wave 3C U-9 (§4.4). How the default burger glyph morphs when the drawer opens: x (default — today's pose, unchanged), x-rotate (the same X plus a 180 degree turn of the whole icon box, dogstudio), line (the top and bottom bars slide onto the middle bar; the travel distance is derived from the icon box via calc(), never a hardcoded px), none (static — no transform at all). Only affects the DEFAULT glyph — `sgs_nav_bar_menu_burger_toggle_markup()`'s own `$is_default_icon` gate (a custom `triggerIcon` has no guaranteed 3-bar shape to morph).

burgerMorphDuration.description: Wave 3C U-9 (§4.4). Burger morph transition duration in ms, 0 to 1200. Default 200 matches today's hardcoded `style.css` value exactly.

burgerMorphEasing.description: Burger morph easing curve, from the shared motion easing list (`includes/helpers-motion-easing.php::sgs_motion_easing_css`, editor `MotionEasingControl`). `ease` is the default. `custom` reads `burgerMorphEasingCustom` (validated; falls back to `ease` when invalid).

burgerMorphEasingCustom.description: Wave 3C U-9 (§4.4). A hand-typed `cubic-bezier(x1, y1, x2, y2)` curve, read only when `burgerMorphEasing` is `custom`. Validated by an anchored numeric regex (four numbers, `-?\d*\.?\d+`, no exponent notation, x1 and x2 clamped to 0-1 by the CSS spec) — an invalid value is REFUSED (never passed through) and the morph falls back to `ease`.

submenuIntentDelay.description: Milliseconds the pointer must rest on a menu item before its dropdown or mega panel opens (0 to 400). Only hover-capable pointers open on hover; touch and keyboard are unaffected.

submenuOpenOn.description: How a dropdown or mega panel opens on a hover-capable pointer: on hover, or only when the item is clicked. Click mode keeps the panel open until it is clicked again, dismissed with Escape, or a click lands outside it. Mirrored by the PHP allow-list in render.php.

attributes._note_three_state_model: Spec 41: every stateful control on this block targets the LINK, in three states — Normal, Hover (:hover, :focus-visible) and Current ([aria-current="page"]). The nav BAR keeps two states (navBg/navColour + their Hover siblings): a bar is never 'the current page'. The submenu PANEL keeps one (FR-41-9): its visibility is a binary open/closed disclosure, so the hoverable surface inside it is the LINK, which carries the full three-state family. Every small string attribute below is declared WITHOUT a JSON enum and is validated in PHP instead: an out-of-enum stored value is silently coerced back to the block.json default with no error, which bites hardest via a programmatic writer (the cloning converter, a theme pattern) setting the attribute directly. The one exception is itemTextDecoration, which carries a real enum — a disclosed asymmetry with its own hover sibling, not an oversight.

itemBgCurrentGradient.description: CSS gradient string painting the current-page nav item's background via the same ::before layer as itemBg; non-empty wins over the flat itemBgCurrent colour.

itemBgHoverGradient.description: CSS gradient string painting the hovered nav item's background via the same ::before layer as itemBg; non-empty wins over the flat itemBgHover colour. It completes the row's three-state gradient set (itemBgGradient / this / itemBgCurrentGradient) and is what the Highlight treatment paints with when the operator picks a gradient (Spec 41 FR-41-25).

itemFontWeightCurrent.description: The non-colour current-page signal (Spec 41 FR-41-6), so the state is distinguishable without relying on colour alone. String, not number — matches itemFontWeight.

itemFontWeightHover.description: String, not number — matches itemFontWeight and itemFontWeightCurrent. A weight change on hover can reflow the bar; the control's help text carries that caution.

itemSmartContrast.description: Opt-in AUTO-FIX: when ON, resolves the item's foreground automatically so it stays readable against whatever background the item is sitting on (Spec 41 FR-41-5). Default OFF: an operator's explicit itemColourHover is respected as-authored — no silent swap. The readability CHECK itself is unconditional and always warns in the editor inspector regardless of this setting; only the automatic colour SWAP is gated on it.

itemBorderWidth.description: Default is OFF (empty object, no border painted) until the operator sets a width. On the horizontal bar this is the ITEM UNDERLINE — a bottom-edge text-indicator under one item's own label. (The drawer list's copy of this attribute family paints the same bottom edge as a ROW SEPARATOR between two adjacent rows.) See nav-menu-css.php's item-border comment for the full reasoning. Not to be confused with itemSeparatorWidth, the independent vertical divider between top-level bar items (FR-41-37).

itemBorderRadius.description: A FLAT corner object of CSS length STRINGS, read by sgs_corner_object_shorthand(), which looks for exactly topLeft / topRight / bottomRight / bottomLeft. NOT the {"desktop":{}} tier envelope — that shape belongs to BLOCK-ROOT radii read by sgs_border_radius_tiers(); used here it would carry no corner keys, the helper would return null, and the radius would silently vanish. Per-element precedent: sgs/product-card::ctaBorderRadius.

itemBorderColour.description: FR-41-36 locked default: underline/row-separator colour at rest (bar: item underline; drawer: row separator — see itemBorderWidth's note).

itemBorderColourHover.description: FR-41-36 locked default: underline/row-separator colour on hover.

itemBorderColourCurrent.description: FR-41-36 locked default: underline/row-separator colour on current/active — same colour as Hover; the absence of a bg fill is what distinguishes Current from Hover.

itemColourHoverTreatment.description: How the item TEXT colour changes on hover: none / swap / sweep. The Sweep option is offered and emitted only when supports.sgs.sweepEligibility.itemColourHoverTreatment passes (Spec 41 FR-41-26). PHP-validated, no JSON enum.

itemBgHoverTreatment.description: How the item BACKGROUND changes on hover: none / swap / highlight. 'highlight' renders the sliding pill, painting from itemBgHover / itemBgHoverGradient (Spec 41 FR-41-25). PHP-validated, no JSON enum.

itemBorderHoverTreatment.description: How the item BORDER colour changes on hover: none / swap / sweep. PHP-validated, no JSON enum.

itemOpacity.description: M-21. Resting opacity (0 to 1) of the top-level item link (and its paired caret glyph). No default — unset emits no opacity rule at all (fully opaque, matching every instance shipped before this attribute existed). Reference: fantasy's top-level items rest at full opacity (unset).

itemOpacityHover.description: M-21. Hover/focus-visible opacity (0 to 1) of the top-level item link (and its paired caret glyph), touch-guarded via sgs_hover_state_rules(). No default — unset emits no rule. Reference: buck/fantasy fade the hovered top-level item to 0.5 (1 to 0.5). Submenu/sublink opacity (fantasy's separate 0.6-to-1 rest/hover pair on `a.menu-sub-link`) is a GENUINELY DIFFERENT value from the top-level item's own opacity on the same reference — reusing this attribute on the sublink would apply the wrong number, so it is scoped to the item element only; see submenuOpacity/submenuOpacityHover below for the sublink's own pair.

itemPaddingShiftHover.description: M-21. On hover/focus, the item's own inline-start padding GROWS by this length: padding-inline-start:calc(<resting inline-start padding> + <value>). Applies to the top-level item link (style.css base 12px) and the dropdown submenu link (nav-menu-submenu-css.php base 16px) -- both read their own resting literal since neither exposes it as a single attribute. Validated through sgs_css_single_length_value(). Empty emits no shift. Reference: halcyon's mega minimal items 14 to 22px; indus-foods dropdown 6 to 12px (a per-site value, set alongside the item's own padding).

submenuOpacity.description: M-21. Resting opacity (0 to 1) of the dropdown/mega submenu link (`.{bem}__sublink`). No default — unset emits no opacity rule at all. Reference: fantasy's submenu links rest at 0.6 — the OPPOSITE direction from the top-level item's own itemOpacity/itemOpacityHover pair, which is why this is a separate attribute rather than a reuse of that one.

submenuOpacityHover.description: M-21. Hover/focus-visible opacity (0 to 1) of the dropdown/mega submenu link, touch-guarded via sgs_hover_state_rules(). No default — unset emits no rule. Reference: fantasy's submenu links brighten to full opacity (1) on hover, from a 0.6 rest — closing the M-21 exit cell the item pair alone could not cover.

sweepAngle.description: Directional sweep angle (FR-41-37) -- standard CSS gradient-angle degrees (0=to top, 90=to right, 180=to bottom, 270=to left), the same convention @wordpress/components's AnglePickerControl uses. Governs the item border/underline Sweep (itemBorderHoverTreatment==='sweep'). Default 90 sweeps left-to-right; 270 sweeps right-to-left. See includes/sweep-css.php.

itemSeparatorWidth.description: FR-41-37 — the independent vertical divider between adjacent TOP-LEVEL bar items (a right-edge rule), separate from itemBorderWidth (the item's own underline/row-separator). Setting itemBorderWidth.right for a vertical divider would share itemBorderColour/Hover/Current with the bottom-edge underline (one colour family, two edges), so it could not be styled independently — this attribute family can. Bar-only (a vertical list has no 'adjacent item' in that axis). No Current state — a between-item rule is not itself a page. Hover treatment (plain colour swap, or a directional sweep) is controlled by itemSeparatorHoverTreatment/itemSeparatorSweepAngle below (see includes/sweep-css.php). Default '' (unset): the divider is invisible until an operator or a cloning-pipeline extraction sets a real value. '' is this attribute's unset sentinel — includes/nav-menu-item-border-featured-css.php gates the whole separator rule on `'' !== $item_separator_width && '' !== $item_separator_colour`, and sgs_css_length_value('') already returns '' — so an empty default cleanly suppresses emission rather than emitting a 0-width rule the gate is not written to expect. A draft with a real separator overrides this default.

itemSeparatorStyle.description: FR-41-37. solid / dashed / dotted / none. PHP-validated, no JSON enum.

itemSeparatorColour.description: Default 'text-muted' (#606D80) measures ~4.7:1 against a cream header background (#FBF3DC), a real WCAG UI-component-border pass (3:1 minimum), while staying visually understated next to the bold 'accent' hover colour. It intentionally differs from the underline/row-separator family's 'border-light' default (#E5E7EB, ~1.12:1 against the same background): a between-item divider and an under-text underline read very differently against the same background.

itemSeparatorColourHover.description: FR-41-37 — Hover-state colour, matching the underline/row-separator family's own Hover token.

itemSeparatorHoverTreatment.description: FR-41-37. How the item separator changes on hover: none / swap / sweep. Sweep is offered and emitted only when supports.sgs.sweepEligibility.itemSeparatorHoverTreatment passes. Default 'swap' is a plain border-right-color change. PHP-validated, no JSON enum.

itemSeparatorSweepAngle.description: FR-41-37. Directional sweep angle for the item separator (same convention as sweepAngle -- CSS gradient-angle degrees). Default 180 (to bottom) is a sensible vertical default for a right-edge divider; shown only when itemSeparatorHoverTreatment is 'sweep'. See includes/sweep-css.php.

submenuColourCurrent.description: Current-page ('you are here') submenu row text colour. Defaults to the `text` token: `text` against `submenuLinkBgCurrent`'s `surface-alt` default measures 14.31:1 on the framework's default palette and 12.55:1 on Mama's Munches (both WCAG AA, verified via wcag-contrast.js maths). A fixed default token, not a runtime contrast computation, so the default does not depend on a contrast-check mechanism.

submenuLinkBg.description: Normal-state submenu row background. Defaults to the palette's cream `surface` token: an explicit, deterministic opaque background means the row always paints its own surface regardless of what colour the surrounding drawer uses, so no runtime drawerBg-aware contrast computation is needed. `text` on `surface` measures 11.86:1 (WCAG AA). Shared by both the bar's dropdown panel and the drawer's nested/accordion submenu (one attribute family, FR-41-36).

submenuLinkBgHover.description: Hover-state submenu row background. Defaults to the brand's `primary` fill. `submenuColourHover` default-closes to `text` at the PHP layer (nav-menu-submenu-css.php), which measures 5.28:1 against this `primary` fill (WCAG AA) — a clear, on-brand hover signal distinct from both the cream Normal state and the Current state.

submenuLinkBgCurrent.description: Current-page ('you are here') submenu row background. Defaults to `surface-alt`, a real framework token every theme.json defines — a subtly raised/alt surface, the same convention a 'currently selected row' uses in an ordinary list. Visually distinct from both the cream Normal row (`surface`) and the solid `primary` Hover fill, while staying closer in tone to Normal than Hover — the standard 'you are here, but not being pointed at' affordance. Paired with `submenuColourCurrent`'s `text` default: 14.31:1 on the framework's default palette, 12.55:1 on Mama's Munches (both WCAG AA, verified via wcag-contrast.js maths).

submenuLinkBgGradient.description: Normal-state gradient sibling of submenuLinkBg; non-empty wins over the flat colour.

submenuLinkBorderWidth.description: FR-41-36 — the submenu ROW's own row-separator border (a horizontal line between two adjacent rows, both in the bar's dropdown panel AND a drawer's nested/accordion-expanded submenu — same mechanism, same selector), distinct from submenuBorderWidth (the PANEL's outer border). Defaults to a bottom-only 1px so an untouched dropdown/drawer-nested row shows the universal always-visible separator.

submenuLinkBorderColour.description: FR-41-36 (C1) — Normal-state row-separator colour token, locked by Spec 41 §FR-41-36's colour table.

submenuLinkBorderColourHover.description: FR-41-36 (C1) — Hover/Current-state row-separator colour token, locked by Spec 41 §FR-41-36's colour table. No separate Current colour: the spec's table gives this row only Normal/Hover language for the separator.

submenuColourHoverTreatment.description: How the submenu LINK text colour changes on hover: none / swap / sweep. Sweep is offered and emitted only when supports.sgs.sweepEligibility.submenuColourHoverTreatment passes. PHP-validated, no JSON enum.

submenuLinkBgHoverTreatment.description: How the submenu LINK background changes on hover: none / swap. Two options only — there is no Highlight on this row. PHP-validated, no JSON enum.

submenuAnimation.description: How every dropdown and mega panel arrives and leaves: none / fade / fade-lift / slide-down / grow. PHP-validated, no JSON enum. Default fade, a pure-opacity transition with no directional assumption, safe regardless of overflow-flip repositioning. Under reduced motion panels open and close whole.

submenuAnimationDuration.description: Opening time of every dropdown and mega panel, in milliseconds, 0 to 3000.

submenuExitDuration.description: Closing time of every dropdown and mega panel, in milliseconds. 0 closes instantly.

submenuAnimationEasing.description: Speed curve for the panels opening and closing, from the shared motion easing list (includes/helpers-motion-easing.php).

submenuAnimationEasingCustom.description: A cubic-bezier() curve, read only when submenuAnimationEasing is custom. Validated; an invalid curve falls back to ease-out.

submenuItemStagger.description: Delay between each item arriving in a dropdown or mega panel, in milliseconds. 0 turns the stagger off.

submenuItemStaggerDuration.description: Each panel item's own arrival time in milliseconds. 0 uses the panel's opening time.

submenuItemStaggerMax.description: Cap on a panel item's delay in milliseconds. 0 means no cap.

submenuItemStaggerDistance.description: How far each panel item travels as it arrives, in pixels. Negative means it falls from above.

submenuBorderRadius.description: The submenu panel's corner radius — the same FLAT corner object shape as itemBorderRadius (topLeft / topRight / bottomRight / bottomLeft, CSS length strings, read by sgs_corner_object_shorthand()). Its default stays EMPTY: the panel already renders its own radius from --sgs-nm-submenu-radius with a token fallback, so there is no behaviour here for a default to preserve.

submenuBorderColourGradient.description: Normal-state gradient sibling of submenuBorderColour; non-empty wins over the flat colour.

submenuShadowColour.description: The shadow's colour. The name is fixed by ShadowControl.js::shadowAttrKeys, which composes it as <base>Colour.

submenuFontSize.description: A {desktop,tablet,mobile} TIER OBJECT, mirroring itemFontSize. There are deliberately no submenuFontSizeTablet / submenuFontSizeMobile siblings: TypographyControls and sgs_typography_css_rule() both branch on whether the stored value is an object and keep all three tiers inside this one attribute, so flat tier keys would have zero writers and zero readers.

triggerMode.description: What the menu button shows: icon / text / icon-and-text. PHP-validated, no JSON enum.

triggerMagnetRadius.description: Pull radius in pixels, 20-400 — the range matches fx-magnet.js's own clamp.

triggerMagnetStrength.description: Pull strength, 2-80 — the range matches fx-magnet.js's own clamp.

burgerColourHoverTreatment.description: How the menu button's ICON/TEXT colour changes on hover: none / swap / sweep. Sweep is offered and emitted only when supports.sgs.sweepEligibility.burgerColourHoverTreatment passes. Governs burgerColour / burgerColourHover (the icon colour), NOT burgerHoverColour (the button's hover BACKGROUND) — the two names are anagram-close and govern different properties. PHP-validated, no JSON enum.

burgerBgHoverTreatment.description: How the menu button's BACKGROUND changes on hover: none / swap. Two options only. Governs burgerBg / burgerHoverColour. PHP-validated, no JSON enum.

scrimColour.description: Backdrop tint colour behind an open dropdown or mega panel: a token slug or hex. Empty means no scrim. Emitted through includes/helpers-scrim.php.

scrimColourGradient.description: Backdrop gradient sibling of scrimColour; non-empty wins over the flat colour.

scrimOpacity.description: Backdrop tint strength per device, 0 to 1. Unset at every tier means no scrim — a bar that never touches this ships nothing extra.

scrimBlur.description: Backdrop blur of the page behind an open dropdown or mega panel, per device, a CSS length. Unset emits no blur.

itemBadgeColour.description: Wave B — background of the optional per-item badge chip ("SOON", "NEW"). Block-level: one colour applies to every badge this bar renders. Badge COPY itself is per-item (the operator's WordPress menu-item Description field, repurposed — includes/nav-menu-markup.php::sgs_nav_shared_badge_html()). Token slug or hex, same shape as sgs/cart's badgeColour.

itemBadgeTextColour.description: Wave B — text colour of the optional per-item badge chip. See itemBadgeColour.

disabledItemIds.description: Wave B — item identifiers (same scheme as featuredItemIds) rendered as non-interactive, non-focusable text instead of a link. Ticked in the Settings tab's Disabled items panel.

itemDisabledColour.description: Wave B — text colour of a disabled item/sublink. Token slug or hex.
